title: Билет в клуб  (A Ticket to the Club)

segments.t: At the rival restaurant, Chef Viktor Barinov scoffs at a chaotic menu combining cuisines from around the world. Meanwhile back at Claude Monet, Vika shares her dinner plans with Max before spotting his concert ticket. Let's listen to their conversation in Russian first.
Меню уже у нас, большое спасибо.
Ну и что тут у нас?
Тут русская, французская и японская кухня.
Они называют это всей кухней мира.
Тут есть пицца, суши и борщ.
Макс, как идут дела на кухне?
Всё хорошо, мы спокойно работаем.
Я придумала блюдо на праздничный ужин.
Это просто здорово, большое спасибо тебе.
Подожди, а это что за билет?
Настя и Костя подарили билет в клуб.
Значит, там только один билет?
Мне готовить сегодня ужин или нет?
Вика, мои друзья меня точно поймут.
Now let's examine this conversation line by line.
Меню уже у нас, большое спасибо.

'We already have the menu, thank you very much.' Chef Barinov uses the classic Russian possession phrasing — literally 'at us' rather than a verb meaning 'to have', pairing it with 'menu' and 'already'.
Ну и что тут у нас?
'So what do we have here?' Chef Barinov uses the classic Russian possession phrasing — literally 'at us' rather than a verb meaning 'to have', followed by 'here'.
Тут русская, французская и японская кухня.
'Here is Russian, French, and Japanese cuisine.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'here' directly with 'Russian', pairing it with 'French' and 'Japanese'.
Они называют это всей кухней мира.
'They call this cuisine from all over the world.' Chef Barinov chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'call' for the ongoing action, followed by 'kitchen' and 'of the world'.
Тут есть пицца, суши и борщ.
'They have pizza, sushi, and borscht here.' Chef Barinov puts the word for 'here' together with 'there is' and 'pizza' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase.
Макс, как идут дела на кухне?
'Max, how are things going in the kitchen?' Here Vika anchors the line on the word meaning 'how' and builds the thought around 'go' and 'things'.
Всё хорошо, мы спокойно работаем.
'Everything is fine, we are working calmly.' The phrasing opens with 'good' before bringing in 'calmly' and 'we work' to make the point clear.
Я придумала блюдо на праздничный ужин.
'I thought of a dish for the holiday dinner.' Vika uses the perfective verb meaning 'thought up' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'dish' and 'festive'.
Это просто здорово, большое спасибо тебе.
'That is simply great, thank you very much.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'just' directly with 'great', pairing it with 'big' and 'thank you'.
Подожди, а это что за билет?
'Wait, what kind of ticket is this?' Vika leads with the direct command form meaning 'wait', followed by 'ticket'.
Настя и Костя подарили билет в клуб.
'Nastya and Kostya gave me a ticket to the club.' Max uses the perfective verb meaning 'gave' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'ticket' and 'club'.
Значит, там только один билет?
'So there is only one ticket there?' Vika turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'then', pairing it with 'there' and 'only'.
Мне готовить сегодня ужин или нет?
'Should I cook dinner tonight or not?' Vika turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'to cook', pairing it with 'today' and 'dinner'.
Вика, мои друзья меня точно поймут.

'Vika, my friends will definitely understand me.' Here Max anchors the line on the word meaning 'friends' and builds the thought around 'definitely' and 'will realise'. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

Caught between his friends' club outing and Vika's romantic birthday dinner, Max promises Vika that Kostya and Nastya will understand if he stays with her.
